how:
Reading the charts

Each bar is how far that input moves the number when it's swapped for an average value. Bars add to 100%; hover for the move in points.

Spreads, totals and team totals

Two regressions on every game since 2016 — one for the margin, one for the total — built from team ratings plus quarterback, weather, rest and injury adjustments (see the Spread and Total charts). Their main job is setting each team's expected points, which drive every touchdown chance and player's volume on the site. Margins typically land within 13 points of the model's number, totals within 13.3.

How much smaller the model's miss is than a player's season or last-three average, on 2021–26 games it hadn't seen. Anytime TD: 8% better than the average guess; interceptions: 2%.

Ranges

Every game is simulated 6,000 times, with teammates sharing one set of team volume so they rise and fall together. Floor and Ceil are the 10th and 90th percentiles (held-out games land inside 78–84% of the time, against 80%). Boom and Bust are the chances of a big or bad game; hover the column for the cutoffs.

Injuries

Out, Doubtful, IR and inactive players are removed and their volume goes to teammates. Questionable players sit in a share of the simulations based on their last practice (did not practice 48% to play, limited 72%, full 85%); their own numbers assume they play, and teammates' numbers already account for the chance they don't.

More detail

Midweek, before game statuses: did not practice 18% to play, limited 66%, full 88%. Early week, before any report: last week's Out players return 31% of the time, Doubtful 45%. Back from injury: eased in at 77–87% of usual volume for one game. Next man up: if a lead back is out and no backup has 25%+ of carries, the top healthy back is added at a 12% carry share. Quarterback changes move receivers' volume and efficiency, not who gets the targets. Listed players get 97% of team volume; the rest goes to depth players.

Prices and DraftKings

Player numbers are the model's own; sportsbook prop prices are no longer pulled (Oct 25), so weeks from Week 8 on show the model alone. Game spreads and totals come from nflverse's free line feed, refreshed every morning. Fair odds are the model's chance as decimal odds, with no house margin. DK pts uses DraftKings scoring (with 3-point yardage bonuses); Value is DK points per $1,000 of salary, Ceil value the same at the 90th percentile.

Terms

Snap %: share of offensive snaps (arrows = 10+ point change last game). WOPR: 1.5 × target share + 0.7 × air-yards share. PPR: 1 per catch, 0.1 per yard, 6 per TD, 0.04 per passing yard, 4 per passing TD, −2 per INT; Std without catches. Quality starts / Duds: games at or above a startable score / at or below a droppable one — description only; they add nothing to the projection.

Steady (0–100, ranked within position among players with 3+ games and a real role: 6+ PPR a game and 10%+ of team targets, 15%+ of carries + targets for backs): half role (how much his share of team targets, carries + targets for backs, moves game to game) and half output (how much his PPR moves). Quarterbacks are rated on output only. Backtest, 2019–2026, prop rungs the model gave about 70–85%: across all players the steadiest third cleared about 2 points more often than the jumpiest third, given the same model chance, but most of that came from fringe players. Among players with a real role the gap was 0.7 points in the fit years and 1.9 in the check years, neither reliable. So read it as a description of how a player's weeks have gone, not an edge. ◆ marks a role change this week (teammate out, trade, return, recent jump or drop in share, a news-named lead back): the score then describes the old role. A label and a filter; it never changes a projection.
